contentfulBlogPost.title: Travel Diary

childMarkdownRemark.html:
Project overview

  • Role: Product Owner, Lead Product Designer & Full-Stack Engineer
  • Team: Solo delivery (end-to-end product strategy, interface design, architecture, and engineering)
  • Platform: Cross-platform mobile (Android distribution via Adobe PhoneGap / Apache Cordova)
  • Core skills demonstrated: Mobile-first UX/UI design, hybrid mobile architecture, hardware API orchestration, defensive systems engineering, local data persistence.

What this project proves about me: I possess the full-spectrum technical and product capability to take a concept from behavioural research and high-fidelity mobile design through to complex hybrid systems architecture, native hardware integration, and a compiled production build.

The challenge

Mobile software is most valuable when anchored to a genuine 'mobile moment'—an activity that is neither practical nor desirable to execute on a desktop or laptop computer. For travellers exploring an unfamiliar city or hiking off the beaten track, recording thoughts, capturing photos, and discovering nearby points of interest must occur immediately, in context, and often under hostile connectivity conditions.

Existing travel tools suffered from three primary constraints:

  1. High cognitive friction: Logging an experience required juggling disparate apps for photography, note-taking, and map navigation.
  2. Network fragility: Most modern travel apps fail completely or block user input when entering network 'dead zones', rendering them useless on trains, remote paths, or roaming connections.
  3. Hardware-software latency: Inefficient hybrid apps introduce severe UI thread 'jank' when accessing native GPS and camera hardware or rendering dense database logs on mid-tier mobile chipsets.

The challenge was to design and engineer a private, responsive mobile diary application that could capture rich memories instantly while surfacing curated, location-aware travel recommendations without degrading device performance.

My process

I followed an iterative, engineering-led product development lifecycle:

  1. User scenario & 'mobile moment' definition: Analysed spontaneous travel behaviours to map critical micro-interactions (e.g. quick note logging on the move, finding nearby attractions while standing on a street corner).
  2. Information architecture & wireframing: Created low-to-high fidelity user journeys in Adobe XD, focusing on ergonomic thumb-zone navigation, single-tap camera activation, and clear visual hierarchy.
  3. Hybrid systems architecture: Formulated the data schemas, asynchronous API orchestration pipelines, and local database storage layers using Apache Cordova/PhoneGap.
  4. Core engineering & native bridge integration: Implemented hardware plugins (cordova-plugin-geolocation, cordova-plugin-camera), integrated third-party cloud RESTful APIs, and established local Web SQL/SQLite persistence.
  5. Defensive optimisation & compilation: Hardened the codebase against network dropped states, conducted memory profiling across Android build targets, and compiled the final Android Package Kit (APK).

What I did

1. Hybrid mobile architecture & UI execution

To achieve cross-platform distribution from a unified codebase without losing access to native device sensors, I opted for an Adobe PhoneGap (Cordova) WebView architecture. I built the client interface using semantic HTML5, modern CSS3, and JavaScript (ES6), backed by Bootstrap components optimised for mobile viewports. Every interactive touch target was sized to meet accessibility guidelines (minimum 48x48 CSS pixels) to prevent mis-taps during movement.

2. Native hardware & API orchestration

I integrated and managed multiple asynchronous services to deliver contextual intelligence:

  • Geospatial coordinates: Accessed cordova-plugin-geolocation to query device GPS hardware with high accuracy parameters.
  • Reverse geocoding: Integrated the Google Geocoding API to asynchronously translate raw latitude and longitude coordinates into human-readable physical addresses.
  • Contextual content discovery: Engineered a dynamic query pipeline leveraging the Google Places API to surface nearby Points of Interest (POIs) and the YouTube Data API to fetch localised video travel guides matching the current geofence.
  • Camera capture: Utilised cordova-plugin-camera to capture photos directly within the entry flow, storing high-resolution image URIs locally rather than holding heavy base64 strings in memory.

3. Local data persistence & performance engineering

Recognising that mobile travellers regularly lose connectivity, I developed a resilient local persistence layer:

  • Indexed storage: Implemented local Web SQL/SQLite database tables with indexed timestamp and location keys, guaranteeing $O(1)$ read complexity during history retrieval and preventing list-scrolling stutters.
  • Fail-soft caching: Built defensive fallback routines. If Google Cloud API endpoints returned rate-limit codes or timed out, the system automatically fell back to cached location strings or surfaced a graceful manual input state without interrupting the user's flow.
  • Lifecycle memory management: Engineered event listeners to terminate background sensor polling immediately after coordinates or images were acquired, mitigating the heavy battery drain common to location-heavy apps.

4. Technical demonstrations

Why I made these decisions

  • Hybrid (PhoneGap/Cordova) over fully native: Choosing Cordova enabled rapid iteration across both Android and iOS targets from a single architectural foundation within a strict five-week delivery window, while Cordova's mature plugin bridge still provided the native hardware access required.
  • Local SQLite/Web SQL over pure remote cloud persistence: Travel journals are fundamentally personal and time-critical. Relying strictly on a cloud database would have broken the app during offline travel. Storing complex entry objects (coordinates, timestamps, strings, and photo URIs) locally guaranteed zero data loss regardless of network connectivity.
  • URI pointers over base64 string storage: Storing base64 image strings directly in the database bloats file size rapidly, causing significant memory overhead and thread stalls in mobile WebViews. Storing lightweight URI references maintained a sub-second query response time and a lean application footprint.
  • Defensive fail-soft state design: Rather than presenting blocking error dialogues when mobile signals dropped, the interface silently defaulted to cached metadata and allowed users to continue drafting entries, preserving their train of thought.

Impact / results

Area Metric / Achievement
Delivery Successfully designed, engineered, and compiled an end-to-end Android APK within a 5-week sprint.
Database retrieval Maintained $O(1)$ query retrieval times across journal logs using indexed Web SQL/SQLite storage.
Resilience 100% offline entry capability achieved; entries created in dead zones persist locally and attach metadata without crashes.
Hardware integration Successfully orchestrated 4 distinct native hardware and external cloud integrations (GPS, Camera, Google Places/Geocoding, YouTube Data API).
Resource efficiency Mitigated background battery drain through selective hardware listener lifecycle management.

Tools and skills applied

Category Tools / skills
Product strategy & UX design User scenario mapping, 'mobile moment' research, Adobe XD, high-fidelity mobile UI prototyping, touch target heuristics
Mobile & front-end engineering Adobe PhoneGap / Apache Cordova, JavaScript (ES6), HTML5, CSS3, Bootstrap, Android SDK build tools
API integration & backend logic RESTful APIs, Google Geocoding API, Google Places API, YouTube Data API, JSON data parsing
Data persistence & architecture Web SQL, SQLite indexing, fail-soft error handling, asynchronous event programming, hardware plugin bridges

Roles performed on this project

  • Lead Product Designer: Defined user journeys, interaction patterns, touch ergonomics, and visual design systems in Adobe XD.
  • Full-Stack Mobile Engineer: Wrote front-end code, integrated native Cordova hardware plugins, engineered the offline database layer, and handled cloud API consumption.
  • Product Owner: Managed the technical scope, evaluated architectural trade-offs, and oversaw compilation and deployment using Android SDK tooling.

childMarkdownRemark.html: Travellers frequently encounter friction when trying to document spontaneous journeys, often struggling with fragmented tools, poor offline resilience, and disjointed location contexts. As sole Product Owner, Designer, and Full-Stack Developer, I designed and built Travel Diary, a cross-platform mobile application engineered specifically around the 'mobile moment' of exploring a new city. Built using Adobe PhoneGap (Cordova), the app synchronises native hardware sensors—including GPS and camera—with the Google Geocoding, Google Places, and YouTube Data APIs. To ensure high performance in low-connectivity travel environments, I implemented a local SQLite/Web SQL indexing strategy and a custom fail-soft caching mechanism. The project yielded a compiled, fully functional Android application capable of sub-second local retrieval, reliable offline journal logging, and seamless context-aware tourist attraction discovery.
